headline: Africa: Sudan: UN, France Condemn Escalating Drone Attacks Across Sudan
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Africa: Sudan: UN, France Condemn Escalating Drone Attacks Across Sudan.
- South Asia: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports.
- Western Russia: Russians kill man in Zaporizhzhia Oblast and attack public transport in Zaporizhzhia for third time in one day – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US Air Force awards Lockheed Martin $694M hypersonic missile production contract.
The Air Force granted Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract in late September for the production and fielding of the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, or ARRW.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Pentagon creates advisory council on human performance, health.
After creating a new directorate on warfighter optimization within the Department of Defense, the Pentagon announced it will form a federal advisory committee to weigh in on issues affecting troop performance and health.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Navy identifies NAS Pensacola sailors killed in car crash.
The U.S. Navy shared the names of the service members who died in a Florida car crash early Saturday morning.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Head of President's Office: Russian defence industry facilities must burn for every victim in Ukraine.
Following deadly Russian strikes across multiple Ukrainian cities on 29 October, the Head of the President's Office has urged the free world to destroy Moscow's ability to wage war.
- The Moscow Times, 5 hours ago: Russian Military Intercepts Record 1.2K Ukrainian Drones Overnight.
Authorities in Ukraine, meanwhile, said a Russian drone attack killed at least 14 people on a train platform in the southeastern part of the country.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russia attacks Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast with missiles, injuring six people.
Russian forces launched a missile attack on the city of Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast on 29 October, injuring six men.

The ECB chief is set to wade back into French politics as her centrist rivals fail to stop the momentum of left- and right-wing populists.

At least 68 people have been killed and dozens more injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, in central Spain’s Toledo province, on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities warned the toll could rise further as rescuers searched the wreckage.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Africa: Op-Ed | Private Interests Threaten South Africa's Tobacco Control Efforts.

Parliament's Health Committee voted in favour of the Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Control Bill earlier this year, allowing it to move forward for a clause by clause review. The proposed law which was meant to prohibit point-of-sale product displays, make public areas fully smoke free and regulate e-cigarettes has reportedly been watered down.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports.
The United States has fired a top military planner, US media reported, with some outlets saying the dismissal was due to the officer allegedly leaking classified information. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, US media reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources. CBS and Fox both reported that Sylvia’s dismissal was related to leaks, with the former citing a Pentagon official as saying the general failed three polygraphs about sharing classified information with the media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election. Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates.

The melting glaciers of Italy's Dolomites are revealing World War I unexploded munitions, drawing attention to a significant European concern as similar remnants emerge across the continent. Countries like Belgium, Germany, and France also grapple with hazards posed by unexploded ordnance during construction and environmental changes. In a notable operation, Italian forces recovered over 250 munitions, underscoring the lasting threat of wartime relics in modern Europe.

Being in a same-sex relationship can make you weirdly invisible. Queer identity shouldn’t be treated as abnormal My boyfriend and I invented a game on our recent trip to Italy. We called it “invisible gays”, which might have been an attempt at some kind of word play around “gays” and “gaze” – but I was on holiday and feeling lazy, so I didn’t push it. The game began when one night he took me out to a little trattoria to celebrate my birthday.
